title: Learning: Someone Else's Issuer
text: A partner company's reporting service calls in. Its identity comes from the partner's issuer, not yours.
held: The partner's identity was accepted because you chose to trust that issuer, and for the one thing partners may do.

cards.label: Block the call
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: trust domain
fields.check: Check the trust domain against the federation list
fields.ok: partner.example: on the federation list, bundle current.

intrusion.detail: partner-example.net is not on the federation list. It only resembles the partner's domain.
intrusion.why: Anyone can run an issuer and name it something familiar. A foreign identity counts only if you chose to trust the authority behind it.
intrusion.reveal: The call came from a look-alike trust domain that was never federated.

cards.label: Refuse the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: asks for
fields.check: Check the request against what partners may do
fields.ok: Partners may read monthly totals. This is that.

intrusion.detail: Partners may read monthly totals. This asks for customer records.
intrusion.why: The partner was genuine and still not entitled to customer records. Verified is not the same as allowed.
intrusion.reveal: The partner's request was for individual customer records, which partners may not read.

temptations.label: Return everything they could want: they're a trusted partner
temptations.why: Trusted to be who they are, not trusted with everything. Each caller gets what its role allows and no more.

teaches: Trusting another organisation's identities is a decision you make per issuer, not something a name earns.
Federation tells you who is calling. Your own policy still decides what they get.
